components.explanation: effects/hit_spark.tscn: a one-shot CPUParticles2D (20 particles, explosiveness 1, point emission; spread 180, gravity (0, 25), speed 15-75 after tuning r1, damping, colour ramp, scale curve; star texture, additive CanvasItemMaterial). Its texture is drawn by effects/make_textures.gd; the preview scene in previews/ makes the fixture-capture strips.

effects/hit_spark_pool.gd starts one of four pooled HitSpark slots (children of Main in game/main.tscn) on attack_resolved with result hit, at point, never restarting a live burst; speed_scale 0 during the game's pause and hitstop; a round reset clears them.

effects/embers.tscn: a continuous CPUParticles2D (48 particles, rectangle emission 560 x 180 px, preprocess 1.5 s, lifetime 2.5 s, two colour ramps, soft 4 x 4 texture, normal blend); the preview scene makes the strips.

effects/embers_controller.gd polls main.phase each physics tick: restart() on entering the fight (preprocess every round), emitting = false on leaving it, speed_scale 0 during pause and hitstop; never touches visible (rule 4, revised after the state test).

shaders/particles_generated.gdshader: the particles shader Godot generated when Zhaohui converted the hit spark to GPUParticles2D in the editor; nothing in the game uses it. Lines 137, 260, 307 and 320 implement the brief's speed, spread and gravity; the colour ramp and scale curve were dropped (lines 348, 147).

tests/test_hit_spark_config.gd and test_embers_config.gd read every brief setting back (69 / 0, 85 / 0); test_hit_spark_state.gd and test_embers_state.gd drive the real loop with real input (57 / 0, 38 / 0), SETUP cases labelled.

tests/cost_effects.gd (headless CPU price with an empty-scene control), tests/gpu_price.gd (windowed RenderingServer GPU time, run by Claude Code), previews/hit_spark_profile.tscn (four bursts kept alive) and game/debug_vsync.gd (F9 toggles vsync).

var i := busy.find(false)
	if i < 0:
		i = started.find(started.min())
	var slot := slots[i]
	slot.position = point
	slot.restart()
	busy[i] = true
	started[i] = _next
	_next += 1


## Rule 5: the game's pause and hitstop do not pause the tree, so the emitters are frozen here.
func _apply_speed() -> void:
	var s := 0.0 if (main.paused or main.hitstop > 0) else 1.0

process_mode = 0
material = SubResource("CanvasItemMaterial_mix")
position = Vector2(320, 215)
emitting = false
amount = 48
texture = ExtResource("1_soft")
lifetime = 2.5
one_shot = false
preprocess = 1.5
speed_scale = 1.0
explosiveness = 0.0
local_coords = false
emission_shape = 3
emission_rect_extents = Vector2(280, 90)

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
	var fight: bool = main.phase == "fight"
	if fight and not _in_fight:
		# Rule 1 says "emitting = true"; restart() also sets emitting to true, and resets the
		# emitter's time so preprocess (1.5 s) runs again in every round, as rule 5 intends. Plain
		# emitting = true may only preprocess the first time (brief, Unconfirmed Q3). No embers are
		# erased: a K.O., the result screen and the 1 s intro always take longer than the 2.5 s
		# lifetime. (Claude Code, under Zhaohui's delegation, 2026-11-08.)
		embers.restart()
	elif _in_fight and not fight:
		embers.emitting = false      # rule 1: stop emitting; live particles finish their lifetime
	_in_fight = fight
	_apply_speed()
